correctness.rationale: Every element of the nontrivial generalized-dihedral coset is an involution adjacent only to the identity in the enhanced power graph. The only additional vertices with that same open neighborhood are the kernel involutions contained in no cyclic subgroup of order greater than two. This false-twin class forces \(m+|T(A)|\) distinct colors, and the universal identity forces one more. An explicit pairing of every remaining kernel vertex with a distinct leaf gives a proper coloring using exactly that many colors, and a nonidentity neighbor distinguishes every repeated-color pair. The invariant-factor formula follows from \(T(A)=A[2]\setminus2A\) for abelian \(2\)-groups and from the existence of an odd-order companion outside the \(2\)-group case.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete exact solution to a published locating-chromatic problem on a natural infinite group family, not a single parameter slice. It covers arbitrary finite abelian kernels, identifies the precise algebraic obstruction through isolated involutions, and converts that obstruction into a closed invariant-factor formula for every abelian \(2\)-group. The ordinary dihedral formula and the elementary-abelian extreme appear as transparent corollaries.
